title: Arcanum Unbounded
description: A comprehensive collection of Cosmere short fiction spanning multiple worlds, introduced with planetary system essays by the in-world scholar Khriss. Includes The Scadrian System (with The Eleventh Metal and Allomancer Jak and the Pits of Eltania), The Selish System (with The Hope of Elantris and the Hugo Award-winning The Emperor's Soul), The Nalthian System, The Rosharan System (with the exclusive Edgedancer novella featuring Lift), The Threnodite System (with Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell), The Drominad System (with Sixth of the Dusk), and the standalone essay The Liar of Partinel. Each story explores a different manifestation of investiture and the fundamental laws that govern the Cosmere, while the essays provide unprecedented insight into the connections between worlds.
archiveDescription: This collection assembles narratives from multiple planetary systems within the Cosmere, each introduced by scholarly essays analyzing the unique magical and physical properties of the respective worlds. The volume includes records from Scadrial, Sel, Nalthis, Roshar, Threnody, and the Drominad system, providing a comparative study of investiture manifestations across different planetary conditions. The accompanying essays represent the most systematic attempt to categorize and understand the underlying unity of Cosmere magic. This accession serves as a reference work for scholars studying cross-world phenomena.

title: Dawnshard
description: Set between Oathbringer and Rhythm of War, this novella follows Rysn Ftori—a young Rosharan woman paralyzed from a fall in her youth who has become a skilled trader and captain. She is tasked with leading an expedition to the mysterious and forbidden island of Akinah, the legendary resting place of a Dawnshard—an ancient Command of such power that it predates the Heralds and the Shards themselves. Navigating political tensions among her crew, the dangerous secrets of the Sleepless, and her own physical limitations, Rysn discovers that the Dawnshard is more than a relic: it is a bond that transforms her into something far more significant than a simple trader. Aided by her bond with the greatshell Chiri-Chiri, Rysn learns that the most important step a person can take is always the next one.
archiveDescription: This supplementary record documents an expedition to the forbidden island of Akinah and the discovery of a Dawnshard—one of the primordial Commands that predate the Shards themselves. The volume follows a young trader's journey across Roshar's eastern seas and her encounter with the Sleepless, ancient guardians tasked with protecting knowledge of immense power. This accession expands the understanding of investiture's deepest origins and the cosmic hierarchy that governs the Cosmere. The events recorded here occur between the third and fourth volumes of the main Rosharan chronicle.

title: Elantris
description: On the world of Sel, the city of Elantris once housed radiant, god-like beings with miraculous powers derived from the Dor—the underlying investiture of the planet. But ten years ago, the Shaod—the transformation that creates Elantrians—broke, transforming people into wretched, undead creatures with unending pain. Prince Raoden of Arelon is struck by the Shaod and thrown into the fallen city, where he discovers a hidden community of survivors and begins to uncover the true cause of Elantris's collapse. Meanwhile, Princess Sarene of Teod arrives for a political marriage only to find her betrothed dead, and the Fjordell high priest Hrathen schemes to convert Arelon by force—or destroy it. Three perspectives converge on the mystery of a broken magic system and the hope of restoring it.
archiveDescription: This volume examines the collapse and restoration of Elantris, the once-legendary city of the Aonic people on Sel. The Shaod—a spontaneous transformative investiture event—had for millennia elevated citizens into god-like Elantrians, but a malfunction in the underlying magical system rendered victims into tormented, undead husks. The record follows three distinct perspectives: a deposed prince trapped within the fallen city, a foreign princess navigating unfamiliar political waters, and a religious zealot pursuing conversion through conquest. The document provides essential insight into the Dor, Sel's unique form of ambient investiture, and the relationship between geographic location and magical function.

title: Oathbringer
description: The Everstorm ravages Roshar and the Fused—the ancient souls of the singers—return to reclaim their world. Dalinar Kholin must confront the darkest secrets of his past as he leads the newly gathered Knights Radiant to the mythical city of Urithiru, the ancient home of the Radiants hidden in the mountains. Kaladin struggles with the crushing weight of command and the loss of those he cannot save, while Shallan's multiple personalities fragment further as she investigates the secrets of the Unmade. As the coalition of monarchs fractures under pressure from the newly empowered Odium, Dalinar's history as the Blackthorn threatens to destroy everything he has built. The third ideal demands that a Radiant swear to seek the truth, even when it means facing the worst version of oneself.
archiveDescription: This record documents the relocation of the Radiant coalition to Urithiru, the ancient tower-city of the Knights Radiant hidden in the mountains of Roshar. The volume examines the deepening conflict with the Fused—the immortal souls of ancient singers—and the psychological toll of command on those who lead the defense. Central to this record is the examination of a highprince's past sins and the nature of redemption. The account provides substantial insight into the Unmade, the influence of Odium on Rosharan history, and the geography of the Cognitive Realm as it manifests around Roshar.

title: Rhythm of War
description: The occupation of Urithiru by the Fused forces of Odium forces the Radiants to wage a desperate guerrilla war within their own fortress. Kaladin, stripped of his Stormlight and bonded to a dying Syl, must protect the wounded spren of the Tower while confronting the deep trauma that has haunted him since his first battle. Navani Kholin, imprisoned alongside the scholars of Urithiru, discovers revolutionary secrets about the nature of Light—Anti-Stormlight, Towerlight, and the fundamental vibrations that underlie all investiture—as she works alongside the brilliant Fused scholar Raboniel. Shallan, Adolin, and their allies venture into the deadly expanse of Shadesmar to prevent the Sibling—the ancient spren of Urithiru—from being destroyed. The science of Roshar reaches a turning point as characters grapple with depression, collaboration with the enemy, and the question of whether peace is possible between humans and singers.
archiveDescription: This volume departs from the battlefield chronicle to focus on the scientific and psychological dimensions of the Rosharan conflict. The occupation of Urithiru by Fused forces provides the framework for a detailed examination of investiture theory, including the discovery of anti-Stormlight and the vibrational nature of all Cosmere magic. The record follows a scholar's collaboration with an enemy researcher, documenting breakthroughs in the understanding of Light, tone, and rhythm. Concurrently, it examines the psychological trauma of prolonged warfare through the experience of a Radiant stripped of his powers. This volume represents a significant advancement in Cosmere scientific knowledge.

title: Shadows of Self
description: The city of Elendel faces a rising tide of chaos as Waxillium Ladrian is called upon to protect the descendants of the Survivor from a threat born of the city's own founding. A series of brutal murders leads Wax and Wayne to uncover a conspiracy involving an enigmatic figure from Scadrial's past—someone who should be long dead. As riots erupt and Harmony's plans remain frustratingly opaque, Wax must confront the limits of his faith in the god who guides him. Marasi Colms, a law student and capable Mistborn in her own right, proves that she is far more than a damsel in distress as she digs deeper into the mysteries of the Set.
archiveDescription: This volume records the destabilization of Elendel's political order as a figure from Scadrial's distant past reemerges in the industrial age. The investigation into a series of ritualistic murders reveals the extent to which Shardic influence continues to shape mortal destinies, even in an era of secular progress. The document examines the tension between technological advancement and the persistent influence of investiture-based phenomena, as well as the growing awareness among Scadrian scholars of a broader cosmological context beyond their world.

title: The Alloy of Law
description: Three centuries after the Lord Ruler's fall, Scadrial has entered a new industrial age reminiscent of the American Wild West, with railroads, electricity, and bustling cities like Elendel. Waxillium Ladrian, a Twinborn—Coinshot and Skimmer—who spent decades as a lawman in the lawless Roughs, returns to the city to claim his noble title after his uncle's death. Alongside his eccentric but deadly partner Wayne, a Feruchemist with a talent for disguises and improvisation, he investigates a series of kidnappings tied to a mysterious new technology. Wax must balance the expectations of high society with his instincts as a lawman, all while confronting a criminal organization known as the Set.
archiveDescription: Three centuries after the cataclysmic events of the first cycle, this record observes Scadrial's transformation into an industrial society. The Elendel Basin has developed into a center of technological innovation, with railways, electricity, and emerging urban culture reshaping the social order. The volume follows the return of a frontier lawkeeper to the city and his investigation into a criminal organization exploiting both old magical traditions and new technologies. This account documents the evolution of Metallic Arts in a changing world and the first signs of external interference in Scadrial's affairs.

title: The Bands of Mourning
description: Wax travels north beyond the borders of the Elendel Basin to the frontier city of New Seran in search of the Bands of Mourning—legendary metalminds said to contain the combined Allomantic and Feruchemical powers of the Survivor himself. Joined by Wayne, Marasi, and the unexpected Steris—whose meticulous planning proves invaluable—Wax uncovers technology created by the Lord Ruler himself and discovers secrets that challenge everything Scadrial knows about the origins of its magic. Beyond the mountains, an ancient temple holds answers about the true nature of the Sovereign, and the threat from beyond the Cosmere grows ever closer.
archiveDescription: An expedition beyond the known borders of the Elendel Basin provides the framework for this record, which expands the geographical and historical understanding of Scadrial. The search for legendary metalminds—reputed to contain the combined powers of the Survivor—leads to discoveries about the Lord Ruler's technological innovations and the true extent of his preparation for future threats. This volume also documents the first substantial contact with artifacts and knowledge originating from outside the Scadrian system, marking a significant expansion in the Cosmere's interconnected history.

title: The Final Empire
description: On the world of Scadrial, the immortal Lord Ruler has oppressed the skaa peasant class for a thousand years under the ash-choked sky of the Final Empire. Vin, a young street urchin who can subtly influence emotions through Allomancy, is recruited by the charismatic rebel Kelsier—the Survivor of Hathsin—to join his crew of Mistings and Mistborn. Together, they plan an audacious heist against the noble houses, targeting the Lord Ruler himself. As Vin trains to master her powers and infiltrates high society, she uncovers secrets about the true nature of Allomancy, the Deepness, and the fragile balance that holds the world together.
archiveDescription: This volume documents the social and magical upheaval that marked the end of the Lord Ruler's thousand-year reign on Scadrial. The world, shaped by constant ashfall and volcanic winter, had been governed under a rigid caste system sustained by the manipulation of metal-born investiture. The narrative follows the formation of a revolutionary conspiracy among the skaa underclass and the rediscovery of Allomancy's full potential as a tool of insurrection. The account provides essential context for understanding Scadrial's political transformation and the cosmic forces that would later emerge from this conflict.

title: The Hero of Ages
description: As the world of Scadrial begins to tear itself apart—ashfalls grow heavier, earthquakes ravage the landscape, and the Deepness awakens—Vin and Elend race against time to discover the true meaning of the Hero of Ages prophecy. Vin must master the power of the Well while resisting its corrupting influence, and Elend, now a Mistborn himself, studies the Lord Ruler's surviving texts for answers. Sazed travels among the Terris people seeking wisdom from forgotten religions, carrying the weight of a thousand faiths. The fate of the entire world hinges on understanding the delicate balance between Preservation and Ruin, and the truth behind the Lord Ruler's millennial reign.
archiveDescription: This concluding record of the first Scadrian cycle details the world's descent toward environmental collapse as the forces of Ruin assert their influence over the physical realm. The ashfall intensifies, earthquakes fragment the landscape, and the very laws of preservation begin to unravel. The volume traces the search for the true meaning of the Hero of Ages prophecy across multiple scholarly traditions, preserved by the Keeper Sazed in his extensive collection of religious texts. The resolution of this crisis fundamentally reshaped Scadrial's geography and established the conditions for the subsequent industrial era.

title: The Lost Metal
description: The finale of the Wax and Wayne era brings threats from outside Scadrial directly to Elendel's doorstep as the Set makes its final move and ancient Shardic rivalries escalate. Wax must reconcile his roles as lawman, nobleman, husband, and father while facing enemies armed with technology and knowledge from other worlds—including a mysterious substance called trellium. Marasi makes discoveries about the broader Cosmere and the true nature of Autonomy, while Wayne faces the consequences of a lifetime of running from his past. Old friends and ancient powers converge for a confrontation that will determine not just the fate of Elendel, but of Scadrial itself in the larger Cosmere.
archiveDescription: The final volume of the second Scadrian cycle chronicles the direct confrontation between Scadrial and external Shardic forces that had been influencing the world from beyond its borders. The substance known as trellium and the involvement of agents from other planetary systems bring the broader Cosmere conflict directly to Elendel's streets. This record documents the maturation of Scadrial as a player in interplanetary politics and the difficult choices faced by those who must balance local loyalties against threats of cosmic scale.

title: The Sunlit Man
description: A mysterious man known only as Nomad—formerly Sigzil, a Knight Radiant of the Skybreakers and Hoid's apprentice—flees across the Cosmere pursued by the relentless Night Brigade. He crash-lands on Canticle, a world that orbits so close to its sun that civilization survives only by constantly moving across the surface on a massive train track, staying just ahead of the scorching dawn. Bound by a Dawnshard that prevents him from harming others, Nomad must use his wits, his spren Auxiliary, and the desperate ingenuity of Canticle's people to survive the planet's tyrannical Cinder King. A race against the sun itself, this story explores the cost of running from one's past and what it truly means to be a man of peace in a universe that demands violence.
archiveDescription: This accession records the experiences of a fugitive from the Rosharan system on the world of Canticle, a planet whose extreme orbital proximity to its sun forces civilization into perpetual motion across a global railway. The document provides valuable data on investiture mechanics across planetary boundaries, particularly the behavior of a Nahel bond and a Dawnshard Command in an unfamiliar investiture environment. The record also offers rare insight into the organizational structures that pursue individuals across the Cosmere and the consequences of the events recorded in the Rosharan chronicles.

title: The Way of Kings
description: On the storm-battered world of Roshar, where highstorms scour the land and everything from plants to creatures has adapted to survive, a war rages on the Shattered Plains between the armies of Alethkar and the mysterious Parshendi. Kaladin, a former battle medic turned slave after being betrayed by his lighteyed master, is sold into Bridge Four—a crew of bridgemen forced to carry enormous bridges into battle as cannon fodder. Across the sea, the brilliant scholar Jasnah Kholin investigates the ancient Knights Radiant and the true nature of the Voidbringers. Highprince Dalinar Kholin, haunted by visions from a power beyond his understanding, struggles to unite the squabbling highprinces as a legendary storm approaches. A slave who cannot be broken, a scholar who pursues forbidden truths, and a warlord seeking redemption converge as the Desolation begins.
archiveDescription: This volume initiates the chronicle of Roshar, a world defined by its violent highstorms and the adaptive biology of its flora and fauna. The record documents the resurgence of the Knights Radiant—orders of investiture-wielding warriors thought extinct for millennia—through the experiences of a slave turned battlefield commander, a scholar pursuing forbidden historical research, and a highprince haunted by visions. The account provides foundational knowledge of Roshar's unique spren ecology, the Surges, and the ancient enmity between humans and the singers known as Parshendi. This is the first in a series of volumes recording what appears to be the return of the Desolations.

title: The Well of Ascension
description: In the year following the Lord Ruler's fall, the newly free city of Luthadel faces chaos on multiple fronts. Three armies converge on the capital: one led by Elend Venture's ruthless father Straff, one by the mysterious invader from the East, and one commanded by a creature of legend made flesh. Vin and Elend struggle to forge a functional government while investigating the Well of Ascension—an ancient source of power said to grant god-like abilities to whoever claims it. Meanwhile, a force deep beneath the city stirs, whispering promises of relief from an ancient burden, and the line between preservation and destruction grows dangerously thin.
archiveDescription: In the immediate aftermath of the Lord Ruler's fall, this record examines the fragile transition of power in Luthadel and the chaos that followed the sudden vacuum of authority. Multiple military forces converge on the capital while the young monarch Elend Venture attempts to establish a constitutional government. The investigation into the Well of Ascension—an ancient repository of investiture beneath the city—reveals the deeper schism between Preservation and Ruin that underpins Scadrial's very existence. This volume is essential for scholars studying post-collapse societal reconstruction and the nature of Shardic influence on mortal affairs.

title: Tress of the Emerald Sea
description: On the oceanic world of Lumar, where twelve distinct types of spore seas—each with dangerous magical properties—cover the planet, a young woman named Tress lives a simple life as a cupwasher on a remote island. When her love Charlie is kidnapped and taken to the Sorceress of the Midnight Sea, Tress embarks on a daring journey across the spore seas, crewed by a motley band of thieves, dragons, and a talking rat. Narrated by Hoid with his characteristic wit and digressions, Tress discovers that courage comes in many forms and that the most unlikely people can become heroes. This standalone adventure explores themes of love, adventure, and the power of determination in a world where even the oceans are alive with danger.
archiveDescription: This unusual accession documents a journey across the spore seas of Lumar, a world where oceanic investiture manifests in twelve distinct types of hazardous spores. The record is framed by the commentary of a narrator whose identity and nature are themselves subjects of scholarly interest. The volume follows a young woman's transformation from an ordinary cupwasher to a captain and explorer, navigating both physical dangers and the complexities of a world where the oceans themselves are alive with latent power. This accession is classified as exceptional due to the narrative's unique framing and the light it sheds on the broader Cosmere's more obscure regions.

title: Warbreaker
description: On Nalthis, magic is fueled by BioChromatic Breath—a resource that can be given away, collected, and used to Awaken objects and command the Lifeless. Princess Vivenna of Idris has trained her entire life for her destiny: to marry the God-King of T'Telir and secure peace for her people. But when her younger sister Siri is sent in her place, both sisters must navigate a dangerous world of divine politics, assassination plots, and the mysteries of the Court of Gods. The immortal Returned god Lightsong questions his own purpose while a mysterious warrior named Vasher—carrying the sentient, soul-devouring sword Nightblood—hunts through the city with his own agenda. The nature of divinity, sacrifice, and what it truly means to give Breath are explored in this standalone tale of two sisters caught in a gods' war.
archiveDescription: This record concerns the world of Nalthis and its unique system of BioChromatic investiture, wherein Breath—a resource that can be voluntarily transferred between individuals—serves as both currency and source of Awakening. The narrative follows the political tensions between the mountain kingdom of Idris and the lowland nation of Hallandren, where Returned gods govern mortal affairs. The volume documents the nature of the Lifeless, the ethical dimensions of Breath commerce, and the existence of a sentient, investiture-devouring weapon of considerable power. The events recorded here have implications for understanding the nature of divine investiture across the Cosmere.

title: White Sand Vol. 1
description: On the dual-faced world of Taldain, where the Dayside is a searing desert and the Darkside is an ocean of black sand beneath a starless sky, the sand masters of the Diem manipulate sand through the power of investiture. Kenton, a young and arrogant sand master, is the sole survivor of a violent coup that destroys the Diem overnight. He must navigate the perilous politics of Lossand, negotiate with the powerful Taishin council, and prove that sand mastery is worth preserving—all while being followed by Khriss, an off-world scholar studying Taldain's unique manifestation of the Dor. The graphic novel format brings the harsh beauty of Taldain to life as Kenton fights for survival in a world where water is more valuable than gold.
archiveDescription: This volume initiates the study of Taldain, a binary planet whose Dayside exists as an unrelenting desert and whose Darkside remains perpetually shrouded in darkness beneath a starless sky. The record documents the sand masters of the Diem, individuals capable of manipulating sand through investiture, and the political upheaval that threatens their extinction. The account is supplemented by observations from an off-world scholar investigating the unique properties of Taldain's investiture system and its relationship to the Dor. This accession provides crucial data on how planetary physics shapes magical expression.

title: White Sand Vol. 2
description: Kenton continues his struggle to rebuild the Diem as the political factions of Lossand vie for control of the sand masters. The discovery of a massive, unnatural sandstorm approaching Dayside threatens everyone, while the mysterious Trackers—agents of the Darkside—close in on their objectives. Khriss and her expedition venture into the treacherous Deep Desert in search of answers about the Sand Lord, the origin of sand mastery, and the connection between Taldain and the wider Cosmere. Alliances shift, secrets are uncovered, and Kenton must decide whether tradition or adaptation will save his people.
archiveDescription: This second Taldain volume continues the documentation of Lossand's political struggles as surviving sand masters attempt to rebuild their order. The record expands to include the Deep Desert and the mysterious forces that dwell within it, as well as the arrival of agents from the Darkside whose objectives remain unclear. The off-world scholar's investigations deepen, revealing connections between Taldain's investiture and the fundamental principles that govern the Cosmere. The volume documents the tension between preservation of tradition and adaptation to changing circumstances.

title: White Sand Vol. 3
description: The conclusion of the White Sand trilogy brings the political and magical conflicts of Taldain to a head. Kenton makes difficult choices about the future of the Diem and his own role in Lossand—must the sand masters remain servants of the Taishin, or can they forge their own path? Khriss uncovers the truth about the Sand Lord, the nature of the Dor on Taldain, and the fundamental principles of investiture that connect all worlds in the Cosmere. The fate of Dayside and Darkside intertwine as Kenton and Khriss discover that the survival of their world depends on understanding the ancient powers that shaped it.
archiveDescription: The concluding Taldain volume records the resolution of the conflict between Dayside and Darkside, and the transformation of the sand master order. The record examines the true nature of the Sand Lord and the origins of sand mastery, revealing connections between Taldain's investiture and the broader Cosmere. The off-world scholar's research yields fundamental insights into the nature of the Dor and its manifestation across different planetary environments. This accession completes the foundational survey of Taldain and its place in the Cosmere.

title: Wind and Truth
description: The conclusion of the first arc of the Stormlight Archive arrives as the contest between champions approaches and the fate of Roshar hangs in the balance. Dalinar faces the terms of his deal with Odium, while Kaladin travels to the realm of the Heralds to understand the origins of the Oathpact and seek a permanent solution to the cycle of Desolations. Shallan journeys into the Cognitive Realm to confront her deepest traumas and unravel the mysteries of the Ghostbloods and her own past. The true history of the Heralds, the origin of the spren, and the dawn of the Cosmere's most significant conflict are finally revealed. Every radiant, every oath, every sacrifice culminates in a battle that will determine whether Roshar survives to see the next sunrise.
archiveDescription: The concluding volume of the first Rosharan arc records the resolution of the contest between Dalinar Kholin and Odium, as well as the journey into the realm of the Heralds to understand the Oathpact's origins. This document provides the most comprehensive account yet of the Cosmere's ancient history, including the true nature of the Dawnshards, the origin of the spren, and the events that led to the current configuration of Shardic influence. The revelations contained herein fundamentally reshape the understanding of Roshar's place in the larger Cosmere and set the stage for conflicts yet to come.

title: Words of Radiance
description: As the Everstorm gathers and the Voidbringer threat grows imminent, Kaladin must master his newfound powers as a Windrunner of the Knights Radiant while protecting the members of Bridge Four. Shallan Davar, a young woman hiding a traumatic past and a fractured psyche, journeys to the Shattered Plains to infiltrate the Ghostbloods and unlock the secrets of the Knights Radiant—including the nature of the Lost Radiants and the true purpose of the Oathgate. The Parshendi prepare to summon the Everstorm, and Dalinar must unite the quarreling highprinces through the ancient code of the Alethi war camps. First ideals are sworn, Shardblades are challenged, and two broken people must learn to trust each other before the world ends. The Radiants have returned—but will they be enough?
archiveDescription: This second volume of the Rosharan chronicle follows the consolidation of the nascent Radiant orders as the Everstorm approaches and the conflict with the Parshendi intensifies. The record examines the Second Ideal of the Radiants and the powers it grants, as well as the political machinations within the Alethi warcamp on the Shattered Plains. A young woman's investigation into the Ghostbloods and her own fractured identity reveals connections between the Lost Radiants, the Oathgates, and the true history of human settlement on Roshar. The volume concludes with a formal challenge to the seat of power itself.

title: Yumi and the Nightmare Painter
description: On the twin worlds of Komashi, Yumi is a revered yoki-hijo who summons benevolent spirits to stack stones into intricate towers for her people—a life of ritual, duty, and isolation. Nikaro, known as Painter, is a loner in a futuristic city who paints nightmares—terrifying entities born of human fear—to trap them before they can harm anyone. When a mysterious force swaps their bodies across worlds, they must learn to inhabit each other's lives and skills to survive. Told through Hoid's framing narrative to his friend Design, this story explores art, purpose, and the beauty of finding connection across the boundaries of culture, class, and reality itself.
archiveDescription: This record concerns the twin worlds of Komashi, presented through a framing narrative of uncertain provenance. The volume documents a unique investiture phenomenon wherein one individual summons spirits to construct stone towers through ritual, while another binds nightmares—entities of concentrated human fear—through the medium of paint. The temporary merging of these two individuals across worlds provides unprecedented insight into the relationship between investiture, perception, and the boundaries that separate planetary systems. The scholarly value of this accession lies in its documentation of investiture systems that diverge significantly from previously catalogued patterns.
